name: אַפַּיִם
summary: A man of Judah in the line of Jerahmeel, son of Nadab and brother of Seled, through whom the line went on: “the sons of Appaim: Ishi” (1Ch 2:30–31). The name is the dual of אַף, the same form as “nostrils” and “face” in “bowed אַפַּיִם אַרְצָה” (Gen 42:6) and “in the sweat of your face” (Gen 3:19, the plural with “your”); scripture does not say why he bore it.

evidence.note: “The sons of Nadab: Seled וְאַפָּיִם; and Seled died without sons.”
The common noun in the same form: Joseph's brothers bowed “אַפַּיִם אַרְצָה”.

note: Takes a.em.ac (the name's two tokens; the brief counts 28 by spelling, the rest being the dual of אַף under a.em.ab). TIPNR records Appaim as a Group, “People from Aph(?)”, but the text presents him as a son of Nadab with a son Ishi, and he is tagged here as a person. The meaning is only the form: the dual “nostrils, face”.
